citations.claim: NS approach N turns green at first violating step 124 during emergency preemption
One step before, N was red and EW was yellow, showing abrupt switch with no all-red
Two steps before, EW was green, so yellow lasted only 1s before NS green

counterfactual.change: Removed the single emergency event (S at t=123); otherwise identical. Without preemption the cycle keeps full yellow and all-red and no violation occurs.

explanation: Emergency preemption immediately forces the emergency direction to green. At step 122 EW was green, at 123 EW yellow with emergency active, at 124 NS green. So EW yellow lasted only 1s (need 6s) and all-red was 0s (need 2s), causing both all_red_clearance and yellow_duration violations. Likely cause: emergency handler switches phase directly to emergency green without enforcing minimum yellow duration and all-red clearance.

violation.detail: approach 0 turned green after only 0 s of all-red (need 2 s)

vision_note: The east-west signals show green in steps 121-122 and switch to yellow for only a single step at 123. At step 124 the north-south signals are already green, with no all-red clearance gap between the directions.
